newsitem.title: USA: Environment worries for new Miami airport.
newsitem.headline: Environment worries for new Miami airport.

text.p: Environmental groups are threatening a lawsuit to force the government to determine the impact the development of a new airport in suburban Miami will have on the nearby Everglades and Biscayne National Parks.

"We need to really look at this and make sure the Everglades restoration and the bay aren't jeopardized" by the development of the Homestead Air Reserve Base, said Sarah Chasis, a lawyer with the National Resource Defense Council in New York.
A lawsuit is "one of the options we are looking at," Chasis said in a telephone interview.

In a controversial move last January, the Metro-Dade County Commission voted to award a long-term lease without competitive bidding for the development of the Homestead Base, located south of Miami. A group of South Florida developers plans a passenger and cargo airport with possible shops, hotels and offices.
A coalition of environmental groups is asking for an environmental impact study and hopes that the White House will announce one in the next few weeks.

"There is not a need for this," said Miguel De Grandy, a spokesman for the airport developers. He said one environmental impact assessment was already done and the "Federal government envisioned all the activities within our plan" when it did the first assesment in 1994.

"The White House is still looking at this issue," said Barry Toiv, a deputy press secretary. He declined to say when the White House and its advisory group, the Council for Environmental Quality, might make a decision.

The environment groups said the White House should be sensitive to this issue because of the multi-billion dollar Everglades restoration project that Vice President Al Gore unveiled with much fanfare here last February.

The new airport would be "a major industrial air pollution source equivalent to an incinerator, power plant or refinery," according to a memo circultaed by the environmental groups. They are also concerned about noise and water pollution.
The developers hope to begin construction before the end of 1997 and are in the midst of securing all the necessary permits, De Grandy said.
Despite a $4 billion expansion plan at Miami International Airport, it will reach capacity in about 2015 and another airport for South Florida will be necessary, De Grandy said.
